content.title: THE FOOD FIX FOR {{BLOATING}} NO ONE EXPLAINS PROPERLY
facts: **Peppermint tea** – relaxes the muscles lining your gut, easing trapped gas and that tight, bloated feeling within 20-30 minutes.
**Ginger** – 1 slice steeped in hot water speeds up stomach emptying, so food (and gas) moves through instead of sitting heavy.
**Papaya** – contains papain, an enzyme that helps break down protein so it doesn't ferment and cause bloating later.
**Cucumber** – 90% water plus quercetin, which calms gut swelling from salty meals.
**Kefir** – 1 small glass/day feeds your gut with live bacteria that outcompete the gas-producing kind.
**Caraway seeds** – chew ½ tsp after a heavy meal, a traditional trick to release trapped air naturally.
**Lemon water** – 1 glass, warm, first thing in the morning kickstarts digestion before your first meal even hits.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
If bloating hits you after almost every meal, a few kitchen staples can help more than you'd think. Peppermint works by relaxing smooth muscle in the gut wall, which is why the pressure and cramping ease so fast after a cup of tea. Ginger speeds up how quickly your stomach empties its contents into the small intestine, so gas doesn't build up and linger. Papaya's papain enzyme actually pre-digests protein for you, meaning less undigested food sits around fermenting and producing gas in your colon. Everyone's gut reacts differently though, so pay attention to what actually settles yours.
